jobDescription: We are a consumer lender that provides unsecured personal loans and credit cards to about 600,000 customers. The Quantitative Risk Analyst develops and monitors the application and behavioural scorecards, prepares model documentation for the independent validation team, runs the monthly model monitoring pack and supports updates to the IFRS 9 impairment models. The model risk policy requires every model developer to hold a master's degree in statistics, mathematics, economics or another quantitative discipline, and the second line checks degree certificates before granting development rights.
requirements: Develops credit scorecards (application or behavioural) using logistic regression or gradient boosting.
Runs monthly model monitoring, including population stability and discrimination metrics.
Prepares model documentation for independent validation.
Holds a master's degree in statistics, mathematics, economics or another quantitative discipline.

evidence.text: Credit Risk Analyst, Fernhill Lending (October 2022 to September 2026): rebuilt the application scorecard for unsecured loans in Python with logistic regression on weight-of-evidence binned features and compared it with a gradient-boosted challenger.

Produced the monthly monitoring pack for six scorecards, with population stability indices, Gini by month of application and the override rate, and raised an alert whenever a model breached its thresholds.
Wrote the development documentation for the rebuilt scorecard (data, sample windows, variable selection, performance and limitations) and responded to the validation team's findings.
Ran the staging-transfer sensitivity tables for the IFRS 9 model refresh and reconciled them with the finance team's provision figures before the quarter-end close.

Education: MSc Financial Mathematics, Larkfield University (part-time, 2024 to 2027), taught modules completed, dissertation in progress, award expected in 2027; BSc Economics, Larkfield University (2022).

Work sample: an anonymised scorecard development summary with the sample windows, the Gini on development and out-of-time samples, the weight-of-evidence charts for the top five variables and the validation team's closed findings.
HR verification note: employment dates and the title Credit Risk Analyst at Fernhill Lending were checked against the payroll record supplied by Fernhill and match the resume.
Reference check summary: the head of credit risk modelling at Fernhill confirmed in writing that the candidate rebuilt the application scorecard and produced the monthly monitoring pack.
